text:
A causal, padding-aware EWMA can maintain numerator and weight states: for each valid interaction, S ← λS + x and Z ← λZ + 1; output S/max(Z, ε). Initialize both states to zero, leave both unchanged on padding, and mask padded outputs. This implements a normalized exponentially weighted prefix average without startup shrinkage. These implementation recommendations follow from the [pandas EWMA definitions](https://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/stable/reference/api/pandas.DataFrame.ewm.html). Use bounded decay, FP32 accumulation, and forward recurrence; avoid formulations dividing by tiny powers of λ. For next-item prediction, the current observed interaction may enter its prefix representation, while its target must remain excluded.

Interaction-index decay measures distance in valid events; timestamp decay measures elapsed time, using λₜ = exp(−ln(2)Δt/half_life). They encode different assumptions and should be compared on validation. Padding must not advance the interaction index. Timestamp decay requires aligned historical timestamps and consistent units; pandas documents the corresponding [time-weighted mean](https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/main/doc/source/user_guide/window.rst). Normalize features independently at each position to preserve causality; normalization statistics spanning future sequence positions would leak information.

For a residual h + g·r, gate magnitude alone cannot measure contribution: residual scale and direction also matter. Suggested diagnostics are ‖g·r‖/(‖h‖+ε), cosine alignment, score changes, and validation ablation with the branch disabled. [ReZero](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.04887) supports zero-initialized residual gates for an identity start. By differentiation, a zero gate initially blocks branch-parameter gradients; keep the branch nonzero so the gate can learn. These are implementation deductions, not evidence of improved recommendation accuracy.
